sections.html:
Fall River is a Bristol County city on Mount Hope Bay, at the mouth of the Taunton River, against the Rhode Island line. The 2020 census counted 94,000 residents, making it the tenth-largest city in Massachusetts. Much of it is built on hillsides that rise sharply from the shore, so a seller on the hill and a seller near the water face different driveways, drainage and foundations.

The city was a leading textile center, and its houses came with the mills. More than 12,000 units of company housing were built for workers, many of them wood-framed tenements and three-floor triple-deckers with up to six apartments. Many still stand, owned by people who live in one unit and rent the rest, or by heirs who never planned to be landlords.

Interstate 195 is the main east-west route. It enters the city over the Charles M. Braga Jr. Memorial Bridge and runs through the middle of the city to Westport. Route 6, MA 138, MA 79, MA 81, MA 177 and MA 24 also serve the city. The highway reaches New Bedford and Cape Cod to the east and Providence to the west, so Fall River works for commuters into Rhode Island, and that widens your buyer pool.

Fall River has a long shoreline, a river and large ponds. The North Watuppa Pond is the main reservoir, and the Quequechan River drops steeply in its last half mile. Before listing, learn your parcel's flood zone from the city or an insurance agent. Lenders and buyers will request it.

If your basement has taken on water, tell buyers plainly and keep any repair receipts. Hillside lots raise a separate question about drainage and retaining walls, which an inspector will look at.

Property taxes are assessed locally, and your bill shows the due dates. Under quarterly billing the installments land on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, and the first one doubles as the abatement filing cutoff. Assessments reflect value as of January 1 before the fiscal year. An abatement succeeds only if you can show fair cash value sits below the assessment, and recent comparable sales are the usual proof.

sections.h2: Before closing: smoke and CO certificate
sections.html:
The Fall River fire department has to certify your alarms, both smoke and carbon monoxide, before the sale. Schedule the inspection once the closing date is set, and expect a fee.

A battery smoke alarm past ten years has to be swapped for a sealed ten-year photoelectric unit. A multi-unit building has more alarms to check, so start early. The deed is also subject to the state's deed excise under chapter 64D, and your attorney will include it on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What local rules should a Fall River seller ask about?
sections.html:
Questions about rental registration, building permits for past work, code enforcement and any open violations belong with city departments.

Before listing a multi-family building, ask City Hall whether any permits were left open, whether the number of units matches city records, and whether the property has any outstanding orders. The buyer's attorney will raise these anyway, and settling them early keeps the closing on track.

Tenants' rights continue after a sale, so tell the buyer about leases and rents up front. Collect each lease, the rent amounts and the move-in dates. A triple-decker with tenants in place can be slow to sell through a listing, because showings need tenant cooperation and some buyers want a vacant unit at closing.

A cash buyer can purchase an occupied building as is, which is why many owners of older multi-families ask for that kind of offer first.

sections.h2: Options for selling a Fall River house
sections.html:
Sellers here tend to pick one of three paths.

  • Listing suits a clean, vacant house with time to spare.
  • A cash offer suits inherited, tenant-occupied or run-down property.
  • Selling by owner suits a seller comfortable with contracts.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Fall River houses as is. Send the address, describe the condition and tenants, and the offer will be explained to you in plain terms. Then weigh it against a listing's net once repairs, commissions and months of waiting are subtracted.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to anyone
sections.html: Collect the deed, newest tax bill, permits, leases and a repair history. For an inherited house, an attorney can say which probate steps must come first. Having these items makes every conversation, with a buyer, an agent or an attorney, faster and more useful.

sections.h2: How the hills and mills affect inspections
sections.html:
A century-old frame building on a slope gets close attention from inspectors. Expect them to look at the foundation and any retaining walls, the porches that tend to hang off triple-deckers, the age of the wiring and the heating system, and each unit's separate utilities. Knowing the answers to these in advance helps you set a realistic price.

Many multi-family owners also have a mix of old and updated units. List what was renovated and when, and keep the receipts. A documented kitchen or a newer boiler counts in your favor with any buyer, cash or not.

With a cash sale you skip open houses, the buyer's repair requests and the wait for a lender. You still handle the same legal pieces: the smoke and CO certificate, any tax balance, the excise tax on the deed and the payoff of any mortgage. Your attorney can confirm each at closing so nothing is missed.

Expect a buyer to ask how old the roof is, when the heating was last serviced, whether any unit has had water damage, and what the rents are. Answer from records where you can. For an occupied triple-decker, tell them which units are leased, for how long and at what rent. Straight answers build trust and shorten the back-and-forth that slows a sale, whether the buyer is paying cash or relying on a bank.

Once an offer is accepted comes the purchase agreement, the fire inspection, payoff of tax or lien balances, and finally the closing, where the deed is signed and recorded. A cash sale can compress this because there is no lender appraisal. A listing depends on the buyer's financing and inspection, so build in extra time if you must move by a certain date. Tell your closing attorney the date as early as you can, and ask what could slow things down in your case, such as a lien, an estate or a tenant, so the date is realistic.

faqs.q: What county is Fall River in?
faqs.a: Bristol County, Massachusetts, on Mount Hope Bay beside the Rhode Island line.

faqs.q: How many people live in Fall River?
Can I sell a triple-decker in Fall River with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Tenants' rights continue after a sale, so tell the buyer about leases and rents. A cash buyer can purchase an occupied building as is.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate in Fall River?
faqs.a: Yes. The fire department issues it for any home sale or transfer, for a fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Fall River assessment?
faqs.a: Send the Fall River assessors an abatement application before the first installment comes due. If they say no, or say nothing for three months, the Appellate Tax Board is the next stop.
